reading.body:
Kevin Hern's AI record is nine political committee contributions from technology companies and four yes votes on bills, with no recorded opposition.

The money is uniform and small. Eight of the nine contributions are $1,000, and the ninth is $4,000 from Microsoft's PAC. The donors are the largest compute buyers and builders: Google three times, Microsoft twice, and once each Amazon, Intel, Oracle, and Anthropic. The dates run from September 2025 to August 2026, so the giving is steady rather than clustered around a vote.

The four recorded votes all passed on motions to suspend the rules, a procedure reserved for uncontroversial bills. That tells you these were not the contested AI fights. The data does not include the bill titles or subjects, so it cannot show whether any vote touched data centers, power, or chip export, which are the questions that matter most for compute.

What this record cannot support is any claim about influence. It shows contributions arriving and yes votes being cast, not that one produced the other, and the page says as much. It also covers only federal filings and floor votes. State legislation, committee work, and private meetings leave no trace here.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Kevin Hern: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 13 events.
